cards.explanation: The answer is that his eyes are too full of conceit. That's the reason David gives. The psalm says, "For his eyes are too full of conceit to detect or hate his own sin." (Psalm 36:2) He can't detect it, and he can't hate it either. I think when you're that full of yourself, spotting your own mistakes gets awfully hard.

The answer is False. The psalm says, "The words of his mouth are wicked and deceitful; he has ceased to be wise and well-doing." (Psalm 36:3) Wicked and deceitful is how David describes the words of the wicked man's mouth. David isn't being gentle here, friends.
The answer is on his bed. David says, "Even on his bed he plots wickedness…" (Psalm 36:4) That's a place most of us go to rest, and he's still scheming. I think this man doesn't clock out.

The answer is True. David says, "he sets himself on a path that is not good…" (Psalm 36:4) Notice who does the setting: he sets himself on it. Nobody pushed him onto that path. The same verse adds that he fails to reject evil.

The answer is the LORD. David turns and says, "Your loving devotion, O LORD, reaches to the heavens…" (Psalm 36:5) He quits talking about the wicked man and starts talking straight to God. I love a turn like that, friends, because it's like walking out of a messy kitchen into a warm one.

The answer is the highest mountains. David says, "Your righteousness is like the highest mountains…" (Psalm 36:6) After reaching up to the sky, he plants his feet on the tallest ground there is. Big, solid and not going anywhere.
The answer is True. David ends the verse with, "O LORD, You preserve man and beast." (Psalm 36:6) People and animals both. God's care covers the whole bunch.

The answer is the shadow of God's wings. David says, "…the children of men take refuge in the shadow of Your wings!" (Psalm 36:7) A shadow like that is a place to tuck in close. I think anybody who's ever wanted somewhere safe to rest would know what that feels like.
The answer is True. David says, "They feast on the abundance of Your house…" (Psalm 36:8) The word is feast, and the word is abundance. Nobody's picking at crumbs there, friends.
The answer is the fountain of life. David says, "For with You is the fountain of life…" (Psalm 36:9) Life itself, and it's with God. I think that's good news for everybody.

The answer is know. David prays, "Extend Your loving devotion to those who know You…" (Psalm 36:10) He's asking God to keep His loving devotion coming to the people who know Him. A prayer like that is a good one to borrow, bakers.

The answer is that David asks God not to let the hand of the wicked drive him away. He prays, "…nor the hand of the wicked drive me away." (Psalm 36:11) He doesn't want to be pushed out. I know a little about being pushed to the back of a drawer, so I get why that prayer matters.

The answer is False. The psalm closes with, "There the evildoers lie fallen, thrown down and unable to rise." (Psalm 36:12) They're fallen and thrown down, and they can't get up. They don't bounce right back, friends.
